procedural_history.originating_court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
procedural_history.impugned_order: Final Order dated 13.09.2018 of the High Court of Judicature at Allahabad in Application U/s 482 - No.36284 of 2017.
procedural_history.high_court_proceedings: The High Court (Single Judge) dismissed an application filed by the appellant under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 (Application No. 36284 of 2017).
procedural_history.supreme_court_posture: The appellant appealed to the Supreme Court because the High Court dismissed their application under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure without properly considering the facts of the case and relevant legal principles. The Supreme Court allowed the appeal, set aside the High Court's order, and remanded the case to the High Court for a fresh decision on merits.

directions: The case is remanded to the High Court for its decision on merits uninfluenced by any of our observations in this order.

issue.issue_text: Whether the High Court was justified in dismissing the appellant’s application filed under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 without applying the principles of law to the factual matrix of the case?

facts: The appellant filed an application in the High Court under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure.
The application sought to quash criminal proceedings initiated against the appellant under Sections 498A, 323, 376 of the IPC and Sections 3 & 4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act.
The High Court's Single Judge dismissed this application.
The appellant then appealed the High Court's dismissal to the Supreme Court.
law: When deciding an application, a court should first set out the brief facts of the case to understand the factual matrix.
The court must then examine the challenge by applying the relevant principles of law to those specific facts.
It is improper for a court to only quote legal principles without referring to or analyzing the facts of the case before it.
application: The Supreme Court examined the High Court's order and found that the Single Judge had extensively quoted legal principles from various decisions concerning the powers under Section 482.
However, the Supreme Court observed that the High Court's order failed to set out the facts of the case or apply the cited legal principles to the actual controversy.
The Supreme Court noted that after reading the High Court's judgment, it was "unable to know the factual matrix of the case."
This failure to connect the law with the facts was deemed an improper exercise and an incorrect way to dispose of the application.
reasoning.conclusion: The Supreme Court concluded that the High Court was not justified in dismissing the application in this manner. Because the High Court failed to apply the principles of law to the factual matrix of the case, the Supreme Court set aside the High Court's order and remanded (sent back) the case for a fresh decision on its merits.

arguments.issue_text: Whether the High Court was justified in dismissing the appellant’s application filed under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 without applying the principles of law to the factual matrix of the case?
appellant_arguments: The High Court erred by not setting out the brief facts of the case to understand the factual matrix before making its decision.
The High Court failed to examine the challenge to the proceedings by applying the relevant principles of law to the specific facts of the case.
The High Court's order was improper as it did not record findings on the grounds urged by the appellant, making it impossible to understand the basis for the dismissal.
respondent_arguments: The respondent's arguments are not mentioned in the provided text.

ratio_decidendi.ratio: When adjudicating a matter, a court must first set out the brief facts of the case to establish the factual matrix, and subsequently, apply the relevant legal principles to those facts to record specific findings on the grounds raised.
obiter: When a case is remanded for a fresh decision, the appellate court should not delve into the merits of the case.

judicial_reasoning.core_finding: The High Court's order was procedurally improper because it only quoted general principles of law regarding Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure without setting out the specific facts of the case, applying the law to that factual matrix, or recording any findings on the grounds urged by the appellant. This omission made it impossible for the Supreme Court to understand the controversy or the basis for the High Court's dismissal.
legal_tests_applied: When deciding an application, a court ought to first set out the brief facts of the case to understand the factual matrix, then examine the challenge made to the proceedings in light of the principles of law, and finally record findings on the grounds urged by the appellant as to whether any interference is called for.
policy_considerations: A judicial order must be reasoned in a way that allows an appellate court to understand the factual matrix and the basis for the decision. An order that merely recites legal principles without applying them to the specific facts of the case is not a proper disposal and cannot be meaningfully reviewed.
